ClientResponses.Response:
Thank you for providing your honest feedback regarding the Spirit E-325 gas grill. Moving from a 2 burner to a 3 burner adds more BTU output, which is why your Spirit E-325 feels much hotter. 

Try these quick adjustments to get back on track. Turn burners down to medium or low after preheating. Leave the middle burner off to create a cooler zone for thicker meats. Download the digital cooking charts directly from Weber website or Weber Connect app. 

If you are still having an issue please reach out to us direct. Our Support team is here to help. Thank you!

Results.ReviewText:
Our first Weber was the largest available back in 2003.  We loved it!  We Then bought two small sized ones for camping and really like them as well. 
We thought Weber name was synonymous with quality so we went with the SpiritE25.  The grill size,  and heating capacity etc is great.  I think the siding and door is not the quality I was expecting.  There is no back to it so storing items below isn't ideal.  There was no gauge for measuring the propane tank and i quickly realized this part is available as an add on.  

Our Spirit E25 came assembled which was a must.
Results.Title: Not the quality of siding as we came to expect.

Results.ReviewText: I bought the spirit e-325 to replace a 16 year old genesis e-310. The genesis was a beast and was still working when itwas retired ( the burners and lid were in bad shape but parts were no longer available). The spirit  e-325 is a little smaller but seems equally well made and is the perfect size for our 2 person family.  I’m still learning the heat settings for different cooks as they are quite different from the larger genesis model but it’s coming along. I do not use the sear settings which seem a little tricked up for me. So far I’ve been quite pleased with the new grill. Time will tell if this model lives up to the durability of the genesis series.
Results.Title: Solid grill for small family

Results.ReviewText: I was never able to use it. It was purchased 9/5/26 online from Home Depot and it arrived with damaged parts. I notified Weber and they said I would get replacements for the parts. But they were out of stock and there was no ETA on when they would be available. I suggested that a new grill be sent to replace it, but was told no. I would have to wait until the parts were available. The ETA finally came on 10/2/26 that said I would receive one of the parts in late October, one in late November, and the last in late December. At that point, I decided that 4 months was too long to wait. I returned the damaged product back to Home Depot and will continue using my old Weber e-610 and just buy some new parts to refurbish it. Bad customer Service for a company that produces such a good product.
Results.Title: Bad Customer Service Solutions

ClientResponses.Response: Thank you for sharing your detailed feedback. We are sorry to hear that the design and mobility of the Spirit E-325 have not met your expectations. We understand your concerns regarding moving the grill, the shelf, and access to the grease management area. Your feedback is valuable, and we will be sure to share your comments with our product team. We appreciate you taking the time to provide your perspective.

Results.ReviewText: Whoever thought that removing two of the wheels is an idiot! It's more difficult to move, and I question how long the shelf will hold up, since it carries all of the weight when you have to move it. I have to move it every time I use it, because the same idiot probably made the decision to not completely enclose the tank area. Raccoons love the free access to the grease drip pan because of this blunder, and I have to store it next to a wall to keep the varmints out. You saved a few bucks to keep the sales price low/pad your margin, but you completely ruined the functionality of what was once a great grill.  Well done Weber!
Results.Title: Idiotic Design
